changes.before: The earth was waste and empty, and darkness was over the face of the deep; and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters.
changes.after: Now the earth was waste and empty. Darkness lay over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters.
changes.reason: Breaks the opening description into two spoken units and preserves both uses of “face” and the edition’s rendering “Spirit of God.”

changes.before: God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Seas. God saw that it was good.
changes.after: God called the dry land Earth, and He called the gathering of the waters Seas. God saw that it was good.
changes.reason: Uses parallel English word order while keeping both naming verbs and the singular gathering.

changes.before: God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars.
changes.after: God made the two great lights, the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.
changes.reason: Makes the stars a separate object of God’s making, outside the enumeration of the two lights.

changes.before: God said, “Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of the heavens.”
changes.after: God said, “Let the waters teem with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of the heavens.”
changes.reason: Represents both the Hebrew swarm verb and its cognate noun, retaining a separate command for the birds.

changes.before: God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. God saw that it was good.
changes.after: God created the great sea creatures and every living, moving creature with which the waters swarmed, according to their kinds. He also created every winged bird according to its kind. God saw that it was good.
changes.reason: Makes the list easier to hear and keeps the waters as the subject of “swarmed.”

changes.before: God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; and rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, and every living thing that moves upon the earth.”
changes.after: God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, and every living thing that moves upon the earth.”
changes.reason: Gives the commands clear breath points and preserves the repeated subject and all five imperatives.

changes.before: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their host.
changes.after: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed, together with all their host.
changes.reason: Connects “all their host” directly to what was completed.

changes.before: On the seventh day God completed the work that He had made, and on the seventh day He ceased from all the work that He had made.
changes.after: On the seventh day God completed the work He had done, and on the seventh day He ceased from all the work He had done.
changes.reason: Uses natural English for doing work and preserves the repeated seventh day and work.

changes.before: These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that YHWH God made earth and heavens,
changes.after: These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that YHWH God made earth and heavens.
changes.reason: Ends the heading here, a reading consistent with Rashi, and preserves the reversal of heavens and earth.

changes.before: when no shrub of the field was yet on the earth and no plant of the field had yet sprouted, for YHWH God had not sent rain upon the earth, and there was no human to work the ground;
changes.after: No shrub of the field was yet on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprouted. For YHWH God had sent no rain on the earth, and there was no human to work the ground.
changes.reason: Makes the two conditions and their explanation clear when read aloud.

changes.before: but a mist would rise from the earth and water the whole face of the ground.
changes.after: But a mist would rise from the earth and water the whole face of the ground.
changes.reason: Begins a new sentence while retaining the contrast and the edition’s rendering “mist.”

changes.before: A river flows out from Eden to water the garden; from there it divides and becomes four heads.
changes.after: A river flows out of Eden to water the garden. From there it divides into four branches.
changes.reason: Conveys the four resulting watercourses named in the following verses.

changes.before: YHWH God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the human, and he slept. He took one of his ribs and closed up flesh in its place.
changes.after: YHWH God made a deep sleep fall upon the human. While he slept, God took one of his ribs and closed the place with flesh.
changes.reason: Makes the change of subject clear while retaining the established rendering “rib.”

changes.before: YHWH God built the rib that He had taken from the human into a woman, and brought her to the human.
changes.after: YHWH God built a woman from the rib He had taken from the human. Then He brought her to the human.
changes.reason: Preserves the distinctive Hebrew verb “built” and gives the second action its own clause.

changes.before: Both were naked, the human and his wife, and they were not ashamed.
changes.after: The human and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
changes.reason: Names the two subjects before describing them.

changes.before: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat from the fruit of the trees of the garden;
changes.after: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees in the garden.
changes.reason: Gives the permission a clear ending before the exception in the following verse. The quotation continues.

changes.before: but from the fruit of the tree in the midst of the garden, God said, ‘You shall not eat from it or touch it, lest you die.’”
changes.after: But about the fruit of the tree in the midst of the garden, God said, ‘You shall not eat from it or touch it, lest you die.’”
changes.reason: Keeps the contrast and makes the woman’s quotation of God easier to follow.

changes.before: The serpent said to the woman, “You surely shall not die!
changes.after: The serpent said to the woman, “You shall surely not die!
changes.reason: Echoes the wording of 2:17 and keeps the serpent’s denial emphatic.

changes.before: The woman saw that the tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining wisdom. She took from its fruit and ate; she also gave some to her husband with her, and he ate.
changes.after: The woman saw that the tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining wisdom. She took some of its fruit and ate. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate.
changes.reason: Gives the actions clear subjects and retains the husband’s presence.

changes.before: The human called his wife’s name Eve, because she was the mother of all the living.
changes.after: The human named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all the living.
changes.reason: Uses a natural English naming formula while preserving the explanation.

changes.before: He drove out the human, and stationed east of the garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the turning sword to guard the way to the tree of life.
changes.after: He drove the human out. East of the garden of Eden He stationed the cherubim and the flame of the whirling sword to guard the way to the tree of life.
changes.reason: Distinguishes the expulsion from the placement of the guards and retains the flame and the sword’s movement.

changes.before: She bore again, his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of the flock, while Cain worked the ground.
changes.after: She gave birth again, this time to Abel, Cain’s brother. Abel became a shepherd of the flock, while Cain worked the ground.
changes.reason: Makes the relationship and second birth clear.

changes.before: but He did not regard Cain and his offering. Cain became very angry, and his face fell.
changes.after: but He did not regard Cain or his offering. Cain became very angry, and his face fell.
changes.reason: Uses normal English negative coordination so both objects clearly fall within the negation.

changes.before: If you do well, will there not be a lifting up? But if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door; its desire is toward you, but you must rule over it.”
changes.after: If you do well, will there not be a lifting up? But if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is toward you, but you can rule over it.”
changes.reason: Retains the lifting image and the echo of 3:16. The modal “can” follows Rashi’s reading of the final clause.

changes.before: YHWH said to him, “Therefore, whoever kills Cain shall suffer sevenfold vengeance.” YHWH set a sign for Cain, so that whoever found him would not strike him down.
changes.after: YHWH said to him, “Therefore, if anyone kills Cain, vengeance will be taken sevenfold.” YHWH set a sign for Cain, so that whoever found him would not strike him down.
changes.reason: Retains the passive form of the warning and the explicit sign for Cain.

changes.before: Zillah also bore Tubal-cain, a sharpener of every tool of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain’s sister was Naamah.
changes.after: Zillah also bore Tubal-cain, who sharpened every tool for working bronze and iron. Tubal-cain’s sister was Naamah.
changes.reason: Reads the tools as implements of the bronze and iron crafts, following Rashi.

changes.before: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day God created humankind, He made him in the likeness of God.
changes.after: This is the book of the generations of Adam. On the day God created the human, He made him in the likeness of God.
changes.reason: Keeps the singular pronoun and connects the collective “human” to the wording of the preceding narrative.

changes.before: Male and female He created them, and He blessed them and called their name Adam, in the day they were created.
changes.after: Male and female He created them. He blessed them and named them Adam on the day they were created.
changes.reason: Keeps the shared name Adam, both creation verbs and the echo of 1:27.

changes.before: and named him Noah, saying, “This one will comfort us in our work and the painful toil of our hands, from the ground that YHWH has cursed.”
changes.after: and named him Noah, saying, “This one will bring us relief from our work and from the painful toil of our hands on the ground that YHWH has cursed.”
changes.reason: Restores the two parallel expressions beginning with “from,” preserving the relation of the toil to the cursed ground.
